claim: Greedy or plain-LLM choice locks onto an early lucky branch and never recovers; sampling from belief or an optimism bonus for untried arms fixes it.
agent_test: Run the tree with greedy vs UCB-style vs Thompson-style branch choice on the same items at equal tokens; count runs where the eventual solving branch was never revisited.
update_d: Gap search: AB-MCTS (Thompson widen vs deepen) is the closest tested LLM tree, but at equal generation calls not tokens, and it is level with repeated sampling on ARC-AGI. RL or SFT trained bandit agents show more early lock-in (d09). Status unchanged.

claim: Off-the-shelf LLMs do not explore in-context: basic GPT-4 prompt shows suffix failure in over 60% of replicates (T=500, N=20); only one of many configs (hint + externally summarised stats + CoT) explored well.
agent_test: Replicate with our model on a 5-arm bandit stub, then on our tree: raw history vs code-computed per-class counts. Same token budget.
update_d: Gap search: new 2025-2026 tests. Raw-history exploit is solved by GPT-5-mini (d04), reasoning models explore far better in an open text game (d05: o1 177, R1 85, GPT-4o 35, humans 42 elements) and exploration correlates with reasoning (d10). But Semantic Bandits (d07) shows label priors still bias a thinking model. Suffix-failure rates for 2025-26 frontier models on the Krishnamurthy bandit were not found. See K20.

claim: Code-computed summaries of tries and passes (not CoT alone) turn exploration on; raw history plus CoT fails.
agent_test: Arm A: raw attempt log in prompt. Arm B: code-computed per-class tries/passes table in prompt. Same tokens.
update_d: Gap search: 2026 frontier agents (35 models) do better with a compact code-built memory than with free reasoning (d06: 76.9 vs 50.0 and 72.2 vs 66.7 as extracted); a summary beats raw history for Qwen3-32B (d07); summaries of readings change re-testing by at most 5 points in Wellocate (d08, a counter-point). Sources 4.

claim: Giving the LLM code-computed UCB statistics at inference helps big models and hard cases, but can hurt small models (Gemma 2B/9B fell 7.6->4.9 and 10.5->4.1).
agent_test: Decide widen in code (UCB on class pass counts) vs ask the model; compare, with model size as a factor if we have two.

claim: Simple tuned heuristics (epsilon-greedy, softmax) match or beat UCB and Thompson in simulation, but only with tuning; badly tuned epsilon degrades fast.
agent_test: Fit the widen threshold on a held-out half of per-class pass data; compare to a fixed default at equal tokens.
update_d: Gap search: heuristics need retuning when rates drift; see K22.

claim: Thompson sampling reaches the Lai-Robbins lower bound for Bernoulli arms and needs no tuned constant, so it is the safe default for a per-class rule.
agent_test: Beta posterior per problem class; sample to pick how wide to search; compare to fixed width. a07 and b28 were not opened.
update_d: Gap search: plain Thompson sampling has high regret under drift (d18); discounted or windowed Thompson is the fix. Status unchanged.

claim: Forward-prediction-error curiosity is hijacked by noise (noisy TV): in a Unity maze the TV drastically slows learning; ICM, RND and reachability-based bonuses resist it.
agent_test: Test a widen signal based on raw diversity of candidates vs one gated on reproducibility (same candidate re-scored gives same check result); measure wasted calls.
update_d: Gap search: RIDE paper adds a MiniGrid noisy-TV where ICM drops (d12); OMNI shows learning progress is lured by boring variations (d19). Sources now 6.

claim: Under injected noise, episodic reachability curiosity (EC/ECO) holds up better than ICM, which can fall below plain PPO (DMLab: PPO 11.6, ICM 7.7, EC 18.7, ECO 28.2).
agent_test: Same as K07; add a noise-injected arm where branch descriptions are paraphrased randomly.

claim: RND-style novelty with a deterministic target gives large gains on sparse-reward games (Montezuma 8,152 vs PPO 2,497), but fails on Pitfall (-3) and is seed-fragile (5 vs 10 seeds disagreed).
agent_test: Use only as a warning: a novelty bonus alone is not enough; measure seed variance of our widen rule over >=10 seeds.
update_d: Gap search: outside Atari, RND/ICM/count stall in procedurally generated mazes (d12: 4th, 3rd, 2nd room for Count, RND, ICM vs all rooms for RIDE); E3B beats them across 16 MiniHack tasks (d13). Both are from authors of competing methods. Gap 9 partly closed.

claim: Dynamics-error bonus does worse than RND in the RNN table (Montezuma 400 vs 8,152, PrivateEye 105 vs 8,666, Venture 0 vs 1,859) but the CNN comparison says Venture, Pitfall and Gravitar are similar; the TV effect is game-specific.
agent_test: Do not claim a uniform noisy-TV penalty; test on our own task mix.

claim: Archive-and-return beats pure intrinsic novelty on sparse reward (Go-Explore Montezuma 43,763 without domain knowledge vs RND 8,152; Pitfall 59,494 mean). Named failures: detachment and derailment.
agent_test: Keep an archive of partial solutions in the tree and restart expansion from the best-scored one vs always from the root. Note scores are not comparable across budgets and need a resettable simulator.
update_d: Gap search: IGE (d21) supports archive-and-return in text puzzles (Game of 24 100% vs classic visitation Go-Explore 38+-22) but at equal environment steps, with deterministic resets. Equal-token cost still unknown.

claim: A bandit over exploration modes, with a sliding window because class rates drift, is a tested design (Agent57, all 57 Atari games above human).
agent_test: Per-class bandit choosing direct vs wide search, window of recent attempts; compare to a fixed mode.

claim: LLMs show a knowing-doing gap in bandits: 87% of rationales compute correct UCB values yet 58% of actions are greedy and 21% optimal; try-all-once is the best prompt-level fix.
agent_test: Force a one-try-per-class pass before any greedy choice; measure coverage of classes.

claim: LLMs have a frequency bias and weak coverage: Gemma2 2B/9B/27B cover 40/65/65% of 10 arms; the 2B model repeats its most frequent action in 96% of picks.
agent_test: Log class-coverage in our tree runs; flag runs below a coverage floor.

claim: GPT-3 shows only rudimentary random exploration, no directed exploration, in the horizon task; its regret equals humans at short horizon.
agent_test: Background only. Model is old.

claim: UCT/MCTS selection over LLM steps helps: LATS HumanEval 80.1 to 92.7; HotPotQA ablations show replacing UCT with DFS lowers EM 0.63 to 0.42; w=0.5 gives 0.55, w=2.0 gives 0.63.
agent_test: Sweep the exploration weight on our tree at equal tokens; check the best w is not the same for each class.
update_d: Gap search: the LATS weight test is HotPotQA only on 100 questions; w=2.0 gives 0.63 which equals the default w=1 (0.63), and w=0.5 gives 0.55. The earlier '0.55 vs 0.63' wording overstated a benefit of w=2.0. Class-dependent best weight untested.

claim: In-context RL works on classification bandits only with stochastic exploration and keeping positive-reward episodes (CLINC150 0.104 naive vs 0.648 vs 0.660).
agent_test: Keep only successful attempts in the context memory vs all attempts. Numbers not re-opened by the cross-checker.
update_d: Gap search: Monea re-opened (d20). Positive-only best for Naive, Stochastic subsampling works with negatives, and the result holds across Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen2.5 0.5B-72B, Gemini 1.5 Flash 8B, so base-model replication is within one paper, not independent.

claim: LLM-defined interestingness filters novelty: Crafter tasks learned: uniform 4, learning progress 55, OMNI 82; 64.9% of ELLM goals were sensible.
agent_test: Judge novelty by a model only when a code check backs it; compare 'model says new' vs 'code says new and check passes'.
update_d: Gap search: OMNI re-opened (d19) and numbers confirmed (LP 55 tasks/9 interesting; OMNI 82/14; success on interesting 0.52 vs 0.78). No independent replication with other base models found.

claim: Regret must grow at least logarithmically in n, so some wasted pulls are unavoidable.
agent_test: Use as a budget sanity check for widening cost.

claim: Reasoning (extended-thinking) models explore much better than non-reasoning ones in an open-ended text task: Little Alchemy 2, 500 trials, elements found: o1 177, DeepSeek-R1 85, humans 42, GPT-4o 35, Llama-70B 25, Llama-8B 9. Exploration quality also correlates with reasoning ability in a second study. No study found that re-measures suffix failure on the Krishnamurthy bandit for 2025-26 frontier models.
agent_test: Run the same tree with the model in thinking mode vs non-thinking plus the code-computed per-class table. Report widen rate, share of runs that never revisit the solving class, and tokens.

claim: A bandit that allocates samples adaptively beats uniform allocation at the same compute: Thompson-based adaptive branching ranks first on MLE-Bench (rank 1.3 vs 2.3 to 3.3) and is level with repeated sampling on ARC-AGI at GPT-4o scale; bandit allocation across queries gives up to +11 points on MATH-500, AIME25 and LiveCodeBench. A per-class rule inside a tree against fixed width at equal tokens is still unpublished.
agent_test: Three arms at equal total tokens: fixed width, progressive widening, per-class Thompson with discount. Report mean pass rate and variance across classes.

claim: When class pass rates drift, plain UCB1 and plain Thompson sampling both degrade; discounted Thompson sampling (gamma about 0.4 to 0.75) and sliding-window UCB (window about sqrt(T log T / breakpoints)) fix this, and a Thompson rule that samples from the last K results of each class needs no exploration constant. Which is better with only a few passes per class is not settled by published data.
agent_test: Replay our own pass-rate history offline: compare discounted TS (gamma grid 0.4 to 0.9), windowed TS (K grid 5 to 30) and SW-UCB on cumulative regret against the best fixed class. Choose window and prior from the replay.

claim: LLM agents misallocate between trying new things and re-checking a noisy result: three of five models spent 75 to 94 percent of slots re-testing, one spent 14 percent, and all lost to scripted rules; a list of untried options helped more than a summary of readings. The re-check rate should be set in code.
agent_test: Set the re-check rate of the check by rule (fixed share, falling with class count) vs let the model decide; compare solved items at equal tokens.

claim: Descriptive labels bias in-context exploration: meaningful arm names reduce exploration, help when aligned with reward and badly hurt when misaligned, and negative rewards trigger more exploration than positive ones. Priors shrink but persist in a thinking model.
agent_test: Show the model class ids as neutral letters vs descriptive names while the widen choice is made by the model; compare widen rates.

claim: For a visit count over idea texts, the safest published measure is the number of meaning clusters (bidirectional entailment with a small NLI model), which was built to ignore paraphrase and beat lexical similarity and sequence entropy (AUROC CoQA 0.77 vs 0.66 for distinct-answer count; TriviaQA 0.83 vs 0.79). Code-embedding cosine above 0.95 is a working near-duplicate filter in program search. Embedding choice can flip the effect of an embedding-based novelty bonus (ImageNet embeddings hurt on one task). No study tests paraphrase invariance of embedding or diversity scores directly.
agent_test: Build 50 pairs of same-idea paraphrases and 50 pairs of different ideas from our logs; measure which of embedding cosine, entailment clustering and compression distance separates them (AUROC) before using any as a visit count.

claim: Learning progress as a widen reward is lured by trivial variations (a noisy-TV in task space): in Crafter it learned 55 tasks of which 9 interesting, while adding an LLM interestingness filter gave 82 and 14. Noise control in older work is to batch several samples per task before computing the gain. Reproducibility (re-check) is the signal the LLM literature has actually measured and found hard for models to manage; reachability-based bonuses were only tested in vision and grid worlds.
agent_test: Feed paraphrase-only variants of a failing candidate into three widen signals (learning progress on the check, re-check agreement, entailment-cluster novelty) and count how often each spuriously triggers widening.

claim: RND/ICM-style novelty bonuses designed for one fixed environment fail or stall in procedurally generated ones (MiniGrid MultiRoomN10S6: Count, RND, ICM reach rooms 4, 3, 2; RIDE all rooms), ICM hurts on Mario once extrinsic reward is added, and ICM falls under a noisy-TV ball. Episodic bonuses (E3B, RIDE) recover this. All comparisons come from authors of the newer method; no neutral replication was found.
agent_test: Use per-item (episodic) counts only; never carry a novelty bonus across items.
